Compute the slope and deflection at the free end of a cantilever beam using Euler-Bernoulli beam theory in N-mm-MPa units.
The beam is fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L, with a downward transverse point load P applied at the free end.
Use the parameters P = 2000 N, L = 1800 mm, E = 200000 MPa, I = 1200000 mm^4.
The bending moment distribution is M(x) = P(L - x), which is PL at the fixed end and zero at the free end. No external couple is applied at the free end.
Calculate the slope at the free end using theta = PL^2 / (2EI) and report the result in radians.
Calculate the vertical deflection at the free end using delta = PL^3 / (3EI) and report the result in mm (downward direction).
Assume small deflections and linear elastic material behavior.
Report the two final numerical values: theta in radians and delta in mm.
